papers.evidence: 以效用为中心的LLM智能体记忆系统，预测未来效用而非过去保真度
papers.tldr: 现有LLM代理记忆系统关注对过去的保真度，但记忆的真正价值在于改进未来响应，保真记忆未必提升效果。Leto将记忆视为预测问题，通过记忆索引保留对话细节，请求时记忆重放提供所需上下文，并用效用循环优化选择。在个性化基准PrefEval上准确率提升16.3个百分点，在长时任务MemoryArena上平均最佳且随链深度增益扩大，在长上下文理解上与原始历史检索相当但服务更少token。该工作表明以效用为中心的记忆设计能更高效地提升LLM代理性能。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on external memory to retain and reuse information across interactions. Existing memory systems treat memory as a record of the past and evaluate it by fidelity to the conversation. However, the value of memory lies in whether it improves the agent's response. A memory system decides what to memorize and what to serve before that response exists, and fidelity checks neither decision against it. Faithful memory can therefore fail to improve the response. We instead view memory as a prediction problem and present \textbf{\emph{\leto{}}}, a memory system for LLM agents that focuses on the utility of memory to the future rather than on its fidelity to the past. Because future requests are unknown, \emph{\leto{}} preserves access to conversation details through memory indexing, allowing information to remain available through its sources. When a request arrives, memory replay draws on this index to anticipate and supply the context the agent needs beyond what the request explicitly states. The utility of the served context remains uncertain until the response is generated, motivating a utility loop that uses response outcomes to refine future memory selection. We evaluate our system against six memory systems on five benchmarks across three scenarios. In personalization, it outperforms the strongest compared memory system by 16.3 percentage points in accuracy on PrefEval and by 3.1 points in task completion on PERMA. For long-horizon tasks, it achieves the best overall performance on MemoryArena averaged over five environments with a gain that increases with the chain depth. In long-context understanding, it is on par with retrieval over the raw history while serving fewer context tokens.

papers.title_en: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
papers.authors: Qingcan Kang, Mingyang Liu, Shixiong Kai, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan
papers.evidence: 基于配对证据路由的记忆冲突治理
papers.tldr: 长期LLM智能体面临过时记忆与变化世界冲突，延迟反馈下局部或全局抑制策略难以抉择。RegimeCouncil以配对证据路由仲裁局部与全局顾问，无需重训练LLM。在LongMemEval等基准30个留出设置中均优于最优固定范围，分歧情节提升5.2-7.3点，集群漂移下提升27.9点。该框架提供记忆冲突在线治理方案，具有优越性和微秒级开销。
papers.abstract_en: Alongside memory storage and retrieval, a fundamental challenge in long-term LLM agent systems is how the agent should act when stored memories conflict with an evolving world. Facts often go stale without explicit deletion, so the conflict surfaces before the store is refreshed: delayed feedback shows that acting on one outdated record hurt, but not whether suppression should stay on that fact (a local policy) or extend to other stored facts (a global policy). Existing systems hard-code one of these scopes at design time. We formulate this online choice, under hidden validity and delayed feedback, as memory conflict governance, and propose RegimeCouncil, a lightweight router that keeps both scopes as advisors and arbitrates between them without retraining the LLM. Each memory-assisted response is scored against a no-memory anchor, by off-path paired comparison or by inverse-propensity estimation from the executed action alone. A Local Advisor tracks only the queried fact, a Global Advisor pools recent outcomes across the store, and an asymmetric Meta Governor follows Local by default, switching to Global only when pooling yields a strictly positive recent utility margin. We prove that using delayed outcomes escapes the prompt-only regret floor, that neither fixed scope suffices alone, and that this margin gate switches within bounded time. On LongMemEval streams, historical drift in TempLAMA and TAQA, delays $τ\in [1, 96]$, and sparse or bandit feedback, with Qwen3-30B-A3B and GPT-4o, RegimeCouncil outperforms the better fixed scope in all 30 held-out settings, by 5.2-7.3 points on disagreement episodes and +27.9 points over standalone cold-start fallback under clustered shifts, while cutting harmful stale-memory use at microsecond overhead.

papers.title_en: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
papers.evidence: 为 LLM 提出具有生命周期管理的参数化记忆系统，包括遗忘机制
papers.tldr: 现有参数记忆方法模仿持续学习，无限期保留信息，难以管理用户记忆生命周期。本文提出参数记忆管理系统，由固定容量LoRA基质（k-hot rank组合，独立时间衰减）和轻量控制器组成，决定记住什么及多久。在长时程用户轨迹数据集上，策略有效平衡回忆与弃权，达到oracle性能的86%，优于CL和RAG基线。这是首个在模型权重中直接管理记忆的系统，为长时程参数记忆奠定基础。
papers.abstract_en: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Our substrate is a fixed-capacity LoRA adapter that consists of k-hot rank combinations which store facts without catastrophic interference and maintain an independently controlled temporal decay, enabling outdated information to fade while long-term facts persist. On this substrate, we train a lightweight controller that governs each incoming user event to ensure the memory system reflects the user's true, updated belief state. To evaluate how memory systems manage user memory, we introduce a controlled dataset of long-horizon user trajectories with varying persistence of facts based on changing belief states and user-behavioral shifts, and probe queries that test recall while information is valid and abstention after it expires. Our policy learns to effectively manage user memory over its entire lifecycle, balancing recall and abstention to achieve 86% of oracle performance, unlike CL and RAG baselines that primarily default to one of the two behaviors. By providing the first system to manage memory directly in model weights, this work establishes a foundation for long-horizon parametric memory.

papers.title_en: NavTTT: Adaptive Parametric Memory via Hierarchical Test-Time Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Luo, Chengxing Lin, Jiaxin Huang, Jiale Liu, Jingyu Guo, Sirui Chen, Aolin Li, Shaoli Huang, Cheng-zhong Xu, Hui Kong
papers.evidence: 通过分层测试时训练为视觉语言导航智能体实现自适应参数化记忆
papers.tldr: 视觉语言导航需长期记忆流式视觉观察，但现有Transformer上下文有限，难以保留长期历史。NavTTT提出导航条件测试时训练，通过自适应参数记忆与分层集成，优先编码信息性视觉证据并构建空间基础记忆。在VLN-CE基准上取得优异导航性能，并在真实机器人上有效执行指令，解决了冗余token干扰记忆的问题。该方法为流式视觉观察的记忆存储提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) demands that agents accumulate and reason over streaming visual observations throughout long navigation episodes. Existing approaches struggle to maintain long-term history, constrained by the finite context capacity of transformer architectures. To solve the problem, fast-weight test-time training (TTT) provides a mechanism for encoding streaming observations into an evolving parameter state. However, existing TTT does not distinguish informative observations from repetitive visual content, allowing redundant tokens to interfere with the retention of information needed for subsequent decisions. We propose Navigation-Conditioned Test-Time Training (NavTTT), which introduces adaptive memory formation and hierarchical memory integration for vision-and-language navigation. NavTTT leverages global navigation context to prioritize informative visual evidence and integrates language instructions with spatial information to construct spatially grounded memory representations. Episode-local nonlinear fast weights store these representations as Adaptive Parametric Memory (APM), preserving history beyond the visual context for later decisions. To reduce cross-layer coupling in memory formation, NavTTT maintains independent fast-weight memories across multiple decoder depths. This decoupled design prevents errors or biases from spreading across different memory levels. Meanwhile, it enables shared historical information to be independently represented at various levels of abstraction. Experiments demonstrate strong navigation performance on VLN-CE benchmarks and effective instruction following on a real robot.

papers.title_en: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding
papers.authors: Changin Choi, Jungwon Park, Jungmin Ko, Jimyeong Kim, Wonjong Rhee
papers.evidence: 为长视频理解智能体设计结构化视频记忆和记忆技能
papers.tldr: 长视频问答需从小时级视频中检索并关联分散证据，现有智能体方法在确定检索内容、选择记忆源及跨时间连接上仍困难。VMSA联合设计结构化视频记忆与记忆技能，构建段字幕记忆、实体事件记忆和实体感知情节记忆三类互补组件，并从成功轨迹中提炼技能库指导检索、推理与验证。在七个基准上，VMSA在三个周长度自我中心任务均最优，Ego-R1 Bench超最强基线9.4%，其余基准最佳或有竞争力。消融证实各组件与技能有效，且技能提升时间证据定位，为长视频理解提供新框架。
papers.abstract_en: Long-video question answering requires retrieving and integrating relevant evidence from videos spanning hours or even days. Recent agentic approaches organize video information into external memories and iteratively retrieve evidence to answer questions. However, effective retrieval and reasoning remain challenging, as agents must determine what information to search for, which memory sources to access, and how to connect evidence across distant temporal intervals. To address these challenges, we propose Video Memory Skill Agent (VMSA), a framework that jointly designs structured video memories and memory skills for long-video understanding. VMSA constructs three complementary memory components. Segment Caption Memory and Entity Event Memory serve as searchable evidence sources, while Entity-Aware Episode Memory provides broad yet detailed video context to guide evidence retrieval and reasoning. To further support effective memory utilization, VMSA induces memory skills from successful agent trajectories, incrementally refining or extending a compact skill library to guide iterative evidence retrieval, reasoning, and verification. Across seven long-video question-answering benchmarks, VMSA achieves the highest accuracy on all three week-long egocentric benchmarks, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 9.4% on Ego-R1 Bench, and the best or competitive performance on four additional benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate the contributions of all three memory components and memory skills, with memory skills also improving temporal evidence localization.

papers.title_en: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
papers.authors: Jiarui Guo, Jinkai Zhang, Yuanhong Yu, Yongchen Zai, Futang Zhu, Ruizhen Hu, Sida Peng, Xiaowei Zhou
papers.evidence: 面向智能体导航的结构化空间记忆
papers.tldr: 现有导航系统常用场景图或图像-文本记录场景记忆，但前者推理开销大，后者无法转化为可执行几何路线。SuperNav-1.5提出结构化空间记忆，由区域分割占用地图和地图接地记忆节点构成，引导探索并提供路线。实验在单目标、多目标和需求驱动导航上均优于基线，路径效率提升显著。该方法支持跨会话重用，并在真实四足机器人上验证，为智能体导航提供了高效记忆方案。
papers.abstract_en: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. Multi-session evaluation demonstrates that the constructed memory can be reused, while deployment on a real quadruped robot further shows the system's applicability.

papers.title_en: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
papers.authors: Jiarui Guo, Jinkai Zhang, Yuanhong Yu, Yongchen Zai, Futang Zhu, Ruizhen Hu, Sida Peng, Xiaowei Zhou
papers.evidence: 提出用于智能体导航的结构化空间记忆，包含区域分割占用地图和记忆节点
papers.tldr: 现有导航记忆方法常采用场景图或图像文本记录，但场景图密集表示给多模态大模型带来较大推理与上下文开销，而图像文本记录无法直接转化为可执行几何路线。针对此问题，本文提出SuperNav-1.5系统，构建区域分割占用地图与智能体维护的接地记忆节点，引导探索未访问区域并提供可执行路线。实验在单目标、多目标、需求驱动导航基准上优于基线，路径效率提升显著，多会话记忆可重用。该系统成功部署于真实四足机器人，验证实际适用性。
papers.abstract_en: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. Multi-session evaluation demonstrates that the constructed memory can be reused, while deployment on a real quadruped robot further shows the system's applicability. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav-1.5/

papers.title_en: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
papers.authors: Xinyu Cao, Tianjie Ju, Zhuosheng Zhang
papers.evidence: 具有记忆程序的递归自进化视觉智能体
papers.tldr: 多模态大模型智能体在查询延迟到探索后的任务中难以保留视觉证据。EvoViM框架将冻结模型自身交互经验转化为一个视觉程序，通过递归追踪失败轨迹并修正丢失或误用证据的操作来演化。在涵盖视觉匹配、空间回忆与顺序决策的六个任务的留出集上，平均分比最强基线AutoMem提高31.3-47.6分。这证明交互经验对视觉证据的保留与使用方式至关重要。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. The program retains images and computes directly on pixels, and its operations decide how this evidence is used in each task. During memory evolution, the same model traces failures in its visual trajectories to the operations that lost or misused evidence and revises them. It also rewrites the notes and analysis tools that guide later revisions, which then build on earlier findings and skip changes that have already failed. We evaluate EvoViM with three multimodal models on six tasks covering visual matching, spatial recall, and sequential decision-making, including three tasks with deferred queries. Across the six tasks, EvoViM improves the average score over AutoMem, the strongest baseline in the main comparison, by 31.3-47.6 points on held-out episodes. Programs written once from the initial environment instructions perform substantially worse, highlighting the value of interaction experience in shaping how visual evidence is retained and used. Code and dataset are available at https://evovim.github.io/.

papers.title_en: HyperHarness: Learning to Generate Personalized Agent Harnesses from User Histories
papers.authors: Zhaoxuan Tan, Jiachen Zhao, Jingbo Yang, Zheyuan Liu, Chuhan Wang, Pei Zhou, Mengting Wan, Meng Jiang
papers.evidence: 从用户历史学习个性化智能体记忆与控制代码
papers.tldr: 现有个性化LLM代理在共享内存工作流与每用户harness优化之间存在权衡：前者高效但无法适应多样历史，后者定制但部署需昂贵搜索且监督稀疏。HyperHarness提出学习共享历史到harness生成器，通过下游任务分数迭代优化，从用户历史直接合成个性化的检索与答案指导代码。在三个基准和三个回答模型上，该方法在九个设置中七项最高，最高提升5.95分，同时将匹配答案tokens减少90.32%。该框架部署时对未见用户单次生成harness，无需每用户任务评分搜索，实现了效率与个性化适应的平衡。
papers.abstract_en: Personalized LLM agents rely on an agent harness, the surrounding memory and control code, to connect user history with downstream decisions. Existing methods typically employ either a single shared memory workflow across all users, which is efficient to deploy but cannot adapt how evidence is retrieved and interpreted across diverse histories, or per-user harness optimization, which customizes behavior for each user but requires costly repeated candidate evaluation at deployment and suffers from sparse, noisy supervision in raw logs. To address this trade-off, we present HyperHarness, a framework that learns a shared history-to-harness generator to synthesize executable, user-specific retrieval and answer-guidance code directly from user histories. Given a user's permitted history, HyperHarness prompts a construction LLM to write personalized retrieval and guidance functions, while downstream task scores across training users supervise iterative refinements to the shared generator without reference harnesses or answering-model updates. At deployment, the frozen generator constructs a harness for each unseen user in a single pass from history alone, eliminating per-user task-scored search. Across three benchmarks (PersonaMemv3, Mem-PAL, and MemoryCD) and three answering models (Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, and GPT-5.6-Luna), HyperHarness achieves the highest aggregate score in seven of nine settings and ranks second in the remaining two, improving over the strongest baselines by up to 5.95 points while cutting matched answer-time tokens by 90.32% over long-context prompting. Analyses show that optimization tailors context allocation to each executor, transfers to unseen user clusters, and amortizes adaptation costs.

papers.title_en: DMC-5: Dual-Model Collaboration with Cache-aware Context Compression for Long-horizon Agents
papers.authors: Haochen Li, Xiaobing Tu, Yinggui Wang, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang
papers.evidence: 长程智能体的缓存感知上下文压缩与双模型协作
papers.tldr: 长程智能体反复输入增长轨迹导致上下文膨胀，传统压缩方法存在信息丢失、语义漂移或成本转移等问题。DMC-5提出非对称双模型协作框架：通用压缩模型维护追加式规范视图并缓存稳定前缀，专用智能体仅处理紧凑决策视图，YAMATO保护关键信息。在AppWorld等基准上，输入减少38.5-57.0%，成本降低14.5-28.0%，性能提升1.0-5.8%。该框架兼顾全局一致性与决策效率，为长程智能体提供可扩展压缩方案。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon agents repeatedly feed an ever-growing interaction trajectory to a specialized agent model. Prefix caching reuses computation over repeated history, but cannot prevent context growth or remove information irrelevant to the current decision. This is especially costly when the specialized agent lacks the cached-input discounts available to general-purpose models, making trajectory compression a natural alternative. However, existing compression methods on selective context risk losing global information, recursively rewriting summary leads to semantic drift, while repeatedly recompressing the full history shifts the growing cost to the compressor. Therefore, we introduce DMC-5 (Dual-Model Collaboration with CaChe-aware Context Compression), an asymmetric framework that assigns full-history integration to a general compression model and action generation to a specialized agent model. DMC-5 maintains the raw trajectory as an Append-only Canonical View, preserving global access while allowing the compressor to reuse a stable historical prefix instead of recursively rewriting or recomputing prior context. The agent operates only on a compact Decision View with recent raw interactions, reducing repeated input while retaining the information needed for the next action. DMC-5 further incorporates YAMATO (integritY-Aware Memory Abstractions for Tool Operations) to preserve execution-critical information during lossy compression. Experiments on AppWorld, OfficeBench, and 8-objective QA show that DMC-5 reduces agent model input by 38.5-57.0% and end-to-end cost by 14.5-28.0% with 78.0-85.0% compressor cache-hit rates, while improving task performance by 1.0-5.8% over the uncompressed baseline.

papers.title_en: COGENT: A Modular Cognitive Architecture for Agentic User Simulation
papers.authors: Yikun Chi, Adam Davies, Debarati Das, Lin Ai, Scott Counts
papers.evidence: 基于ACT-R的认知架构，显式包含记忆模块
papers.tldr: 标准计算机使用代理聚焦任务完成，难以复现人类感知、推理与行动方式。COGENT提出模块化认知架构，借鉴Norman行动环与ACT-R理论，将模拟过程分解为感知、记忆、用户状态、意图与动作选择等模块。在AgentNetBench、A11y-CUA和SENSE-42三个基准上，COGENT相较计算机使用基线取得显著保真度提升，并恢复人类自报心理状态的关系结构。该工作验证了可解释、可干预、模块化LLM认知模拟的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based user simulation can support interface design, accessibility research, and interactive-agent evaluation, but standard computer-use agents are optimized for task completion rather than reproducing how people perceive, reason, and act. We introduce COGENT (COGnitive agENT), a modular cognitive architecture for simulating user interaction with desktop interfaces. COGENT draws on established cognitive theories, such as Norman's action cycle and ACT-R, to enable explainable, intervenable, and modular user simulation by decomposing the simulation process into cognitive modules with explicit representations of perception, memory, user state, intentions, and action selection. We begin by presenting six intervenability demonstrations, each tracing how a single edit to memory, a user attribute, or a processing module propagates through the cognitive pipeline to produce a behavioral change. We evaluate COGENT's behavioral and attributional fidelity across three benchmarks -- AgentNetBench, A11y-CUA, and SENSE-42 -- finding that it achieves statistically significant fidelity gains over computer-use baselines in reproducing recorded human behavior and recovers the relational structure among human self-reported psychological states. Together, these demos and evaluations demonstrate COGENT's utility toward more faithful, explainable, intervenable, and modular LLM-based cognitive simulations.

papers.title_en: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
papers.authors: Ruijie Ma, Haoyue Liu, Mingda Zhang, Dongxu Yue, Xiaoying Tang
papers.evidence: 具身问答中覆盖约束的视觉记忆构建与维护
papers.tldr: 具身问答需从历史视觉观察中提取证据，但观察序列增长、视角质量差异和计算资源有限使紧凑记忆构建困难。CoverMem通过覆盖约束选择满足对象质量与场景代表性的全帧，并在新观察到达时仅局部更新受影响帧。同时采用预算内互补帧选择平衡问题相关性、支持度与冗余。在三个基准上，该方法在有限视觉预算下提升问答性能，为预算化具身问答提供高效记忆方案。
papers.abstract_en: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that locally reselects only the affected frames to satisfy updated coverage requirements as observations arrive; and (3) a budgeted complementary frame selection method that balances question relevance, additional support for question requirements, and redundancy with selected frames within a fixed budget. Experimental results on three benchmarks covering diverse environments and question types demonstrate that CoverMem improves question-answering performance under limited visual budgets.

papers.title_en: Internalized Experience: How Training Data Shapes Memory Formation in LLMs
papers.authors: Xianxuan Long, Xinnan Dai, Kai Guo, Jiliang Tang
papers.evidence: 研究LLM中参数化记忆的形成与训练数据的关系
papers.tldr: 大语言模型通过参数记忆保存经验并复用规则，但训练数据如何塑造规则内化尚不清楚。论文提出FSMem状态转移框架，构造训练数据并评估规则复用。实验发现，行动类型多样性增加会阻碍规则学习，扩大状态-行动覆盖通常有利，单深度训练导致深度特化，而累积短长轨迹语料能以更少tokens超越仅长轨迹训练。这些结果揭示了执行经验构造影响规则内化，为优化参数记忆的训练数据设计提供指导。
papers.abstract_en: Parametric memory enables large language models (LLMs) to retain information from past experience and reuse it in subsequent tasks. Yet how training data supports the internalization of reusable task rules remains unclear. We introduce FSMem (Finite-State Machine Memory), a state-transition framework for constructing training data and studying how data content and organization shape memory formation. We evaluate rule reuse across synthetic worlds, classical planning, and code execution through valid-action identification and execution-outcome prediction, complemented by next-operation prediction in code. Our experiments reveal several systematic learning patterns. Under matched training conditions, even unchanged task rules become harder to internalize when learned alongside a larger variety of action types; by contrast, scaling the training data to provide broader state-action coverage generally improves rule learning. We further find that training at a single execution depth produces depth-specialized behavior, with models performing best when training and test executions have similar lengths. Motivated by this finding, we construct cumulative corpora that combine short and long trajectories, which can outperform long-trajectory-only training while using fewer training tokens. Together, these results demonstrate that the same task rules can be internalized differently depending on how execution experience is constructed, and that understanding these learning patterns can guide the design of more effective training data for parametric memory.

papers.title_en: FORGETMENOT: Auditing Memory Driven Privacy Risks in Commercial AI Agents
papers.authors: Ismat Jarin, Tu Le, Athina Markopoulou
papers.evidence: 审计商业 AI 智能体中长期记忆的隐私风险
papers.tldr: 商业AI代理引入长期记忆以增强个性化，但存储、披露、透明度和删除控制的隐私风险缺乏系统审计。本研究提出FORGETMENOT框架，收集约3800个多轮会话（约600万tokens）分析五个流行代理。结果发现代理存储大量个人敏感属性，用户可见记忆比实际少约20%，删除后仍存在泄漏，Gemini对第三方泄露率达31.9%。这些发现揭示显著隐私风险，为设计改进和监管建议提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Commercial AI agents increasingly incorporate long-term memory (both persistent and chat-history) to enable more accurate and personalized responses, raises significant privacy and policy concerns. Yet little is known about user privacy risks associated with memory behavior, in particular, about memory storage, disclosure, transparency and deletion control. To bridge this gap, we propose FORGETMENOT, an auditing framework for analyzing the privacy risks of long term memory in commercial AI agents. Using our framework, we collect around 3800 multi-turn sessions comprising around 6M tokens across five popular AI agents. Our results show that agents store a wide range of personal attributes, including demographics, health, and sensitive details. Furthermore, user visible memory reveals substantially less (around 20% on average) attributes than the agents store in practice, exposing a significant transparency gap. Our stealth memory injection (SMI) technique further increases the amount of personal and sensitive attribute stored in memory, raising it by 25% and 15% for Copilot and Claude, respectively. We further observed memory deletion control is unreliable, as all five agents exhibit non-zero post deletion leakage, including health and self-harm related attributes. Finally, we demonstrate the feasibility of memory disclosure to a 3rd-party email recipient as a proof-of-concept, as Gemini shows 31.9% leakage rate. Together, our findings reveal notable privacy risks in commercial agents memory. Finally, we discuss both design implications and regulatory recommendations to protect users memory privacy in commercial agents.

papers.title_en: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect - KV Cache Management for AI Agents
papers.authors: Shashwat Jaiswal, Chloe Alverti, Mengmei Ye, Chen Wang, Hubertus Franke, Fan Lai, Tianyin Xu, Josep Torrellas
papers.evidence: 面向AI智能体的KV缓存管理与预测预取
papers.tldr: LLM智能体交替执行推理与工具调用，重复使用不断增长的上下文，导致KV缓存工作集远超GPU内存，检索延迟成为瓶颈。TripleKV提出三层KV缓存管理系统，利用工具感知延迟预测器提前从SSD预取所需KV块到主机DRAM，避免占用GPU内存。该系统在多种智能体上大幅减少关键路径SSD读取，P95首token时间最多降低49%，优于现有系统。TripleKV有效隐藏了检索延迟，提升了高并发下智能体的推理性能。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents alternate between inference and tool execution, repeatedly reusing their growing context across calls. Under high concurrency, their combined key-value (KV) cache working set can reach hundreds of GiB, far exceeding GPU memory capacity. As idle KV cache blocks are evicted to slower storage tiers, returning agents incur expensive retrievals that stall inference.   To address this problem, we present TripleKV, a three-tier KV cache management system that hides the delays of these retrievals. In agentic workloads, the KV blocks needed by the next inference request are known in advance; only the time of their reuse is uncertain. TripleKV uses a tool-aware latency predictor to estimate when each tool call will complete and prefetches the required KV blocks from SSD into host DRAM ahead of time. Unlike GPU prefetching, this avoids reserving scarce GPU memory and interfering with concurrent inference requests. To further improve DRAM utilization, TripleKV eliminates duplication of GPU-resident blocks in DRAM, and introduces a victim-cache mechanism that refills blocks from SSD upon their eviction from GPU memory.   Across data, web, and coding agents, TripleKV reduces the fraction of requests requiring critical-path SSD reads from 45-76% to under 10%. It also reduces P95 time to first token (TTFT) by up to 49% compared with vLLM extended with DRAM and SSD KV-cache tiers, and achieves 1.5-7$\times$ lower P95 TTFT than recent agent-aware systems.

papers.title_en: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice
papers.authors: Qingxu Fu, Xuanfa Jin, Ziqian Chen, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding
papers.evidence: 通过引导练习构建肌肉记忆，结合 OODA 内循环与递归自改进
papers.tldr: 推理模型决策延迟高，难以用于亚秒级交互控制；快决策模型又缺乏新任务的细粒度经验。System-One RSI借鉴运动学习，构建在线高频OODA循环与离线递归改进循环，无需专家演示和仿真，仅用少量真实回合将经验固化为外部肌肉记忆。在Snake、绝区零、黑神话悟空三个游戏环境中，27B决策模型取得显著提升。该框架为交互式智能体提供了低延迟、可自我改进的新路径。
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning models provide strong multimodal task understanding but struggle with sub-second control because deliberation increases decision latency. Fast decision models can meet the response window, yet prompting and few-shot examples do not readily provide the fine-grained experience required by a new task. Inspired by coached motor learning, this paper presents System-One Recursive Self-Improvement (System-One RSI), which couples two loops. The high-frequency online inner loop is an Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) cycle: a decision model maps each visual observation and task question to structured judgments, and a decision tree converts them into timed actions without invoking a reasoning model. The offline outer loop is a recursive improvement cycle carried out by a team of reasoning agents. The team revises the decision-model prompt and decision tree, captures interaction records, derives supervision from those records, and trains or deploys updated model parameters. The improved system then returns to the environment and generates the experience for the next round, consolidating learned distinctions as external muscle memory. The framework operates with a small number of real episodes, without expert demonstrations, environment modification, sandboxing, or parallel simulation. Experiments in Snake, Zenless Zone Zero, and Black Myth: Wukong use a 27B decision model. Mean Snake score increases from 1.30 to 7.35. In an evaluated scenario of Zenless Zone Zero, median completion time decreases by 8.4%. In an evaluated combat scenario of Black Myth: Wukong, the evasive policy achieves 11 times the mean survival time of a stationary reference, while the offensive policy win rate rises from 0% to 66.7% across the evaluated configurations.
